newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM threatens force in airwaves dispute.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM threatens force in airwaves dispute.

text.p: Cambodian Co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Monday threatened to call out tanks against Cambodia's Information Ministry unless state media gave the prince and his royalist party more air time.

"If they don't broadcast today, the tanks will come out. I speak frankly. They will really come," said Ranariddh, who ordered the Secretary of State for Information Khieu Kanharith to air statements by his FUNCINPEC party.
Ranariddh earlier said he had six tanks under his control that he was willing to use to fight "complete anarchy in the media".

Ranariddh, who was speaking at a school opening in eastern Cambodia, has complained that state media are biased in favour of co-Premier Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP), and has accused Information Minister Ieng Mouly of not giving equal coverage to his royalist FUNCINPEC party.
Ieng Mouly recently formed an alliance with the rival CPP.
Ranariddh appeared irritated in particular that state television did not broadcast FUNCINPEC's annual congress last week or press statements by his party.
At the congress, Ranariddh declared the ousting of Ieng Mouly would be one of the party's top priorities.
Ranariddh's threats against Ieng Mouly were likely to exacerbate tensions between Ranariddh and Hun Sen. The two leaders formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.

Most recently, they have been feuding over the role of royalists in politics. Hun Sen has said he wants members of the royal family to renounce their royal status if they enter politics, an idea Ranariddh has angrily rejected.
Later on Monday, a grenade thrown from a passing car exploded outside Ieng Mouly's Phnom Penh residence, injuring a taxi driver.
Police said the incident was not politically motivated but the result of lovers' quarrel, and police chief Mak Chito said a man had been detained in connection with the attack.
Ieng Mouly could not be reached, but his wife said the grenade exploded outside the front gate on Monday evening. Ieng Mouly was not at home at the time of the attack, she said.
